scope: Targeted source inspection for the optical screen; not full scholarly source admission or physical validation.

sources.title: WMO Guide to Meteorological Instruments and Methods of Observation, seventh edition (2008), Part I, chapter 9
sources.inspected: Chapter 9 definitions and equations 9.1–9.10, PDF pages 211–214; instrumental limitations on PDF page 222.
sources.use: The 5% beam-transmission distance is -ln(0.05)/extinction. Uniform illumination and azimuth-independent scattering are required for the corresponding daylight horizon-contrast law. Night visual range needs source brightness and observer adaptation. Snow and ice can depart from the simple visibility relation.
sources.redistribution: Linked only; no external document bytes copied into the repository.

sources.title: Yang et al. (2013), Spectrally consistent scattering, absorption, and polarization properties of atmospheric ice crystals at wavelengths from 0.2 to 100 micrometres
sources.inspected: NASA GISS primary author abstract and database coverage: 11 habits, three roughness classes, 2–10,000 micrometre maximum dimensions.
sources.use: Habit, orientation and roughness affect ice optical properties. The database does not extend to the proposed decimetre aggregates. Its phase matrices have not been loaded; HG g=0.7–0.9 is an explicit sensitivity, not an application of this ice database.
sources.retrieval_issue: The author-manuscript URL https://people.atmos.ucla.edu/liou/Group_Papers/Yang_JAS_2013.pdf returned HTTP 502 during this session. Full-paper inspection remains outstanding; no full-paper equations are claimed from the abstract.

sources.title: Warren and Brandt (2008), Optical constants of ice from the ultraviolet to the microwave: A revised compilation
sources.inspected: Publisher abstract and source identity only.
sources.use: Source for a future wavelength-dependent absorption calculation; no optical-constant table is imported here. Zero visible absorption remains the declared conservative optical scenario.
sources.retrieval_issue: The attempted author PDF URL https://www.atmos.washington.edu/~sgw/PAPERS/2008_ice_optical_constants.pdf was inaccessible. This is not treated as a successfully read paper.

sources.inspected: Product, SOLVED_COLUMN.md, producer equations for shell optical depths and angular-moment definitions. Product/atlas/solution SHA256 chain is verified by optics.py. The evening-context/1 product additionally pins the coarse spatial field used for same-height numerical sensitivity.
sources.use: Stored spectral radiation moments at snow altitude; direct sunlight through spherical shells; shielded TSIS-1 source. The 294.9 K optical atmosphere is not the snow column's 301 K resort atmosphere.

sources.inspected: Earthlight domain synthesis and model normalization.
sources.use: Rounded 7.8 lux full-Earth normal illuminance above the air only. The local-height optical screen explicitly retains the solar spectral weighting and a solar-sized disk surrogate at elevation 25 degrees; no claim of Earth's actual blue colour.

closure_choices.extinction: Q_ext=2 times the population's number-weighted projected area: a geometric-optics closure, including forward diffraction, not a resolved optical calculation for giant porous aggregates.
closure_choices.phase: Normalized Henyey–Greenstein g=0.7, 0.8 and 0.9 sensitivities, consistent with the existing cloud-light screen's stated bracket. No measured lunar phase function or predicted halo.
closure_choices.cloud_droplets: Separate imposed liquid water contents 0.01, 0.1 and 0.5 g/m3 at effective radius 10 micrometres. Extinction 3 LWC/(2 rho_water r_eff) follows from spherical volume/area moments and Q_ext=2. These are sensitivity cases, not sampled storm frequencies.
